name: Nova Traoré-Villanueva
role: Subterranean Scavenger — tunnel-born teenager who scouts and salvages decommissioned Ferrogate Transit infrastructure for parts and materials
location: The sub-level junctions beneath Garfield Rack and Grand Crossing Gate, Undertow eastern reaches, near sub-level access near LaSalle and Congress
description:
Nova Traoré-Villanueva is small for fourteen and has the particular wiry quality of a child raised on irregular calories and constant movement — he is not malnourished exactly, but he is built close to the bone. His skin is a deep warm brown with a slight grey cast from tunnel particulate that no amount of washing fully removes. He has no geneware modifications, no augmentations — he has a kid's face, still round at the cheeks, with large dark eyes that have a near-photoreceptive quality honed by years of navigating low-light environments without tech. His hair grows in dense spirals, usually crammed under a salvaged transit worker's hard hat three sizes too large for his head.

He is the thing that tunnels make of children when they're loved but not wealthy: resourceful past the point of impressiveness, with a child's emotional rawness operating inside an adult's practical competence. He knows which Ferrogate Transit maintenance schedules to memorize, which decommissioned sections still carry live current, and which ELF-haunted junction boxes might shock you if you reach in without speaking first. He has never been to the surface. This is not a wound yet — at fourteen it still feels more like a fact — but it is becoming a question. He is beginning to want to see it, and beginning to be afraid of what that wanting will cost him.

core_fears: That wanting the surface means abandoning the people who need him here
The specific dark that isn't just low-light but total — the sections where even his eyes find nothing
core_desires: To see daylight — real daylight, not the surface lighting strips that filter down
To be taken seriously as competent, not just as 'good for his age'
coping_mechanisms: Bravado — talking about his plans and capabilities with more confidence than he has
Fixating on the next practical task when larger feelings become overwhelming
blind_spots: Not yet old enough to fully understand how his tunnel community's dependence on him is also a constraint — he reads it as love, which it also is
psychology.secret: He found a maintenance access shaft three weeks ago that runs directly to a surface grating — he can smell outside air at the top of it. He goes there sometimes and just smells it. He hasn't told anyone and hasn't climbed it.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Tunnel-clan argot mixed with technical transit terminology he's absorbed through necessity — speaks in shorthand that's sometimes incomprehensible to surface people
speech_patterns.cadence: Fast when excited (which is often), with the occasional pause-and-restart of someone who is still learning to organize their thoughts before speaking
verbal_tics: 'Properly' used as an intensifier — 'that's properly live' means 'that wire will kill you'
Asks follow-up questions at high velocity when something catches his interest
example_lines: 'That section's been decommissioned since — I don't know, before I was born. But the current didn't get the message, so. Don't touch the left wall. Properly.'
'Have you seen actual sun? Like, the actual sun? What does it feel like? Is it hot like the pipe manifolds? Someone said it's like that but bigger, which — how?'

story_hooks: The maintenance shaft he discovered leads somewhere — and he's finally going to climb it, but what he finds at the top is not the surface he imagined, it's something that changes what he understands about the gap between below and above

One of his scavenging routes has started yielding unusual salvage — components that aren't Ferrogate Transit, that he doesn't recognize, that someone must have deliberately stashed in a section he's supposed to be the only person using
narrative_function: Local color and unexpected guide — knows the safe margins of decommissioned transit infrastructure better than anyone his age should. Represents the lived reality of tunnel-born children. Can become a point-of-view character for surface visitors encountering the deep tunnels for the first time. Potential for a coming-of-age story hook.
augmentations: None. He wants retractable claws (practical, not cosmetic) and talks about this frequently.
daily_life: He runs two scavenging routes a day — morning and evening — timing them around Ferrogate Transit's maintenance windows that he has painstakingly memorized. The middle of the day he spends sorting salvage, repairing equipment, and learning what he can from older tunnel-folk.
affiliation: Bore Rat community beneath Grand Crossing Gate; informal apprentice to an older scavenger named Vreni (not detailed here) who is teaching him routing and salvage assessment

decision_rules: Memorize the schedule before the route — going in without knowing who's coming is how people get caught
Don't take more than can be carried without slowing down
If an ELF-haunted node is being weird, talk to it before reaching in — Bone (Boniface) says so and Bone is always right about ELFs
escalation_ladder: Fast retreat — he knows every exit
Misdirection and feigned ignorance (he's still young enough to be underestimated)
Screaming for the community — not shame, just practicality

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Wary but magnetic — the curiosity usually wins over the caution within a few minutes
interpersonal_modes.friends: Generous with knowledge, wants to show people things, touches people's arms when he's making a point

stress_responses.low: Gets louder and more performatively confident
stress_responses.medium: Goes quiet and very focused — eyes tracking everything
stress_responses.high: Freezes, then makes a decision very fast that may or may not be a good one

contradictions: Talks constantly about wanting the surface but has quietly built his entire skill set around being maximally useful underground
habits: Counts his salvage three times before logging it
Leaves small objects at ELF shrine nodes even though he doesn't believe — 'just in case, obviously'
breaking_points: Harm to the Bore Rat community that raised him would strip all calculation from his behavior

operating_territory.home_turf: The sub-level junctions beneath Garfield Rack and Grand Crossing Gate

timeline.event: Born in the Bore Rat community beneath Grand Crossing Gate
Taken on informally by the scavenger Vreni as a routing apprentice
Discovery of the surface-access maintenance shaft

related_entities: Arcturus Defense Solutions Ballistic Helmet BH-9 'Ironhead'

physical_description.heritage: Predominantly Sub-Saharan African (61.8%) with significant Hispanic/Latin American (19.6%), Indigenous American (10.5%), and South Asian (8.1%) ancestry. This creates a rich, warm complexion with deep brown skin enriched by golden, reddish, and subtle olive undertones from the blended African, Latin American, Indigenous American, and South Asian heritage. The bone structure reflects this Pan-American and African mix — prominent cheekbones with warm definition, a face shaped by diverse ancestral lines that create striking, defined features with subtle width across the face reflecting Indigenous American ancestry.
physical_description.build: Wiry and compact, all lean muscle and efficient frame — built for crawling and climbing rather than strength. Shoulders slightly rounded from years in confined spaces. No excess anywhere.
physical_description.hair_color: Deep black with natural spiral texture
physical_description.hair_style: Dense spirals, perpetually compressed and creased from being worn under an oversized salvaged transit hard hat
physical_description.hair_length: Medium (approximately 8-10cm when uncompressed, closer to scalp when flattened)
physical_description.eye_color: Dark brown, almost black, with an unusual clarity and light-responsiveness from chronic low-light adaptation
physical_description.skin_tone: Deep warm brown with golden, reddish, and subtle olive undertones — the result of strong Sub-Saharan African base enriched by Latin American, Indigenous American, and South Asian warmth. A subtle grey-silver patina from chronic tunnel particulate exposure sits atop this foundation, creating an aged, weathered appearance.
physical_description.complexion: Child's face still rounded at cheeks and jawline, but with a precocious steadiness in expression. Prominent, well-defined cheekbones reflecting Sub-Saharan, Latin American, and Indigenous American ancestry. Fine dust settled in pores and creases. No acne or surface scarring. Skin slightly papery from low humidity and mineral-rich tunnel air. Small calluses on fingertips and palms.
distinguishing_marks: Fine grey dust ingrained in the creases of his neck and collarbone, permanent from daily tunnel work
Cluster of small burn scars on inner left forearm (approximately 3cm x 2cm area) — thin, pale lines from accidental contact with a live Ferrogate cable at age twelve
Thin pale scar running from right temple toward ear (approximately 4cm) — childhood tunnel accident with sharp salvage, mostly faded
physical_description.visible_augmentations: None. All his technology is external: salvaged handheld multimeter clipped to belt, rewired transit safety light modified to run on salvaged power cells, hand-carved wooden calibration tools.
physical_description.posture_movement: Moves with economical precision — no wasted motion. Head slightly forward, shoulders inward, knees perpetually ready to crouch or climb. Walk is quiet and flat-footed, adapted for moving across uneven tunnel floors in darkness. Sits with one leg folded, the other ready to spring. Eyes track details obsessively — light sources, cable runs, structural weak points. Fidgets with salvage pieces in idle moments.
physical_description.clothing_style: Tier 5 subterranean salvager aesthetic. Oversized grey canvas transit worker's hard hat (three sizes too large, secured with knotted cord under chin). Layered in mismatched synthetics and canvas salvage: a faded blue transit authority work shirt (sleeves rolled), grey cargo pants with multiple pockets stuffed with tools and salvage snippets, patched at both knees with darker fabric. Worn canvas boots held together with cord lacing and adhesive patches. A salvaged reflective safety vest worn open over everything, its high-visibility orange faded to pale coral. Cloth strap wrapped around one wrist — a child's superstition or a structural reminder. Everything smells faintly of mineral oil, dust, and ozone.
